governance_requirements.summary: Changing either freeze-map list requires an Architecture Council decision with written rationale.
Any lane touching a listed anchor must declare owner, phase, status bucket, validation gate, and rollback owner.
A freeze-in-C anchor stays blocked from direct Zig bridge or port claims until a parity scorecard entry exists and the Architecture Council records why the status can change.
If validation is incomplete, contradictory, or weak, the code stays in C and the blocker must be recorded.

gaps.why_now: The live freeze map existed, but it needed explicit governance rules so freeze-in-C and study-only status changes are no longer implied by momentum alone.
A Phase 15 lane note keeps the new governance rule reviewable beside the roadmap instead of hiding it inside a small doc edit.
The shared Phase 15 build gate is the smallest honest way to keep the freeze-map governance slice runnable.
The convenience target keeps the Phase 15 governance slice aligned with the rest of the repo's bounded phase gates.
The next honest Phase 15 step is a small parity scorecard starter so a future status-change request has a concrete comparison artifact rather than only policy language.
